question: If Z follows standard normal distribution with mean 0 and variance 1, then Z² follows:

options.text: Chebyshev distribution with degree of freedom 1
Beta distribution with α = 1 and β = 1
Normal distribution with mean 0 and variance 1
Gamma distribution with α = 1 and β = 1

solution:
The correct answer is **Chebyshev distribution with degree of freedom 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• If Z follows a **standard normal distribution**, then Z² follows a chi-square distribution with 1 degree of freedom.
 
• The chi-square distribution is a family of distributions that is used to model the sum of the squares of independent standard normal random variables.
 
• The distribution is characterized by the degree of freedom, which is the number of standard normal variables that are squared and summed.
 
• F or a chi-square distribution with 1 degree of freedom, the distribution is known as the Chebyshev distribution.
 
• The Chebyshev distribution has a mean of 1 and a variance of 1. It is a right-skewed distribution with a peak near 1 and an exponential tail.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Chebyshev distribution** has important applications in the fields of engineering, mathematics, and statistics.

 
 
• For example, it is used to model the distribution of the maximum absolute value of independent standard normal random variables.
 
• It is not the same as the standard normal distribution.
 
 
 
• The standard normal distribution is symmetrical and bell-shaped, while the Chebyshev distribution is right-skewed and has a peak near 1.
 
• The Chebyshev distribution is a special case of the chi-square distribution.
 
• The** chi-square distribution** has more degrees of freedom and is more flexible, but it also requires more information to specify.
 
• The Chebyshev distribution is a useful distribution for modeling the behavior of extreme values in a data set.
